history.heading: Colony and slavery
paragraphs: Guadeloupe is an archipelago in the Lesser Antilles, its main island shaped like a butterfly formed by Basse-Terre and Grande-Terre. It was inhabited by Kalinago people, who called it Karukera, "island of beautiful waters". Columbus named it after a monastery in Spain in 1493.

France colonised Guadeloupe in 1635 and developed sugar plantations using enslaved Africans. Slavery was abolished during the French Revolution in 1794, but Napoleon restored it in 1802, crushing resistance led by Louis Delgrès. It was finally abolished in 1848. Indentured workers from India arrived afterwards.

history.heading: Overseas department
paragraphs: Guadeloupe became an overseas department of France in 1946. In 2009 a general strike of several weeks protested against the high cost of living, and unrest occurred again in 2021. Contamination of soil and water by the pesticide chlordecone, used on banana plantations, is a major health issue.

culture.heading: Creole culture
paragraphs: French is official, and Guadeloupean Creole is spoken by most people. Culture blends African, French, Indian and Caribbean influences. Gwoka, drum-based music and dance, is recognised by UNESCO, and zouk music became popular across the Caribbean and Africa.

Carnival is a major celebration. Creole cuisine includes colombo (a curry), accras (fritters) and rum, of which Guadeloupe is a renowned producer. The Mémorial ACTe in Pointe-à-Pitre commemorates slavery.

politics.heading: Part of France
paragraphs: Guadeloupe is an overseas region and department of France and part of the European Union. It has a regional council and a departmental council and elects members to the French parliament. There are debates about greater autonomy.

economy.heading: Economic structure
paragraphs: The economy depends on public services, tourism, and agriculture, especially bananas, sugar cane and rum. Most goods are imported from mainland France, and the cost of living is high. Unemployment, especially among young people, is much higher than in mainland France. The currency is the euro.
